keyVerseText: And they were all amazed at the mighty power of God. But while they wondered every one at all things which Jesus did, he said unto his disciples,
rootMeaning: The root of μεγαλειότης (megaleiótēs) is μεγαλεῖος (megaleîos), which conveys the idea of great things or wonderful works. This root suggests not only physical greatness but also a sense of magnificent perfection and conspicuous favor. Thus, the word μεγαλειότης carries a depth beyond simple majesty or power; it embodies an impressive and splendid greatness that is both awe-inspiring and indicative of divine excellence.
usageInScripture: The term μεγαλειότης appears three times in the New Testament and early first-century writings, consistently translated as majesty, magnificence, or the mighty power. Its usage highlights a range of divine attributes, from the overwhelming power of God to the splendor and glory associated with His presence. This consistency in translation underscores the word's role in expressing God's transcendent greatness and glory in a way that commands reverence and awe.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding μεγαλειότης enriches our comprehension of God's nature as revealed in Scripture. It emphasizes not only God's power but also His majestic splendor and glory, which together affirm His supreme authority and worthiness of worship. This term reminds believers that God's greatness is multifaceted—manifesting in mighty acts and in His radiant glory. Recognizing this majesty fosters a deeper reverence and trust in God's sovereign rule and His perfect works, central to a Christ-centered faith that acknowledges Jesus as the ultimate revelation of God's magnificence.
keyVerseReflection: Luke 9:43 speaks of those amazed at the mighty power of God, a phrase where μεγαλειότης conveys more than mere strength; it captures the awe-inspiring, majestic power at work through Jesus. This word enriches the verse by highlighting that what the people witnessed was not just power but a divine magnificence that caused wonder and amazement. It invites believers to reflect on the glorious nature of God's works in Christ, inspiring faith rooted in the recognition of God's splendid and mighty presence.
